questions.question: Rollovers happen when drivers:
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns at too high a speed. Always take turns and curves slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Bobtail tractors are ____ to stop than tractors attached to full semitrailers.
questions.explanation: Bobtail tractors have no semitrailer attached. They are harder to stop and need more distance to come to a complete stop than a tractor pulling a loaded semitrailer.

questions.question: ____ are the cause of more than half of all accident-related truck driver deaths.
questions.explanation: More than half of all truck driver deaths from accidents are caused by truck rollovers. To prevent rollovers, load cargo low and centered on your truck. Take corners slowly and carefully.

questions.question: Pull out the trailer air supply control to test:
questions.explanation: Test the trailer emergency brakes before every trip. First, make sure the trailer rolls freely. Then pull out the trailer air supply control or put it in the "emergency" position. Pull forward slightly and confirm the trailer does not move.

questions.question: An air supply control lever should be in its "normal" position when you are:
questions.explanation: Older vehicles may have levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. When the air supply control is in the "normal" position, it is set correctly for pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Before backing your tractor under the trailer, make sure your trailer brakes are:
questions.explanation: When coupling a trailer, it is important to follow the correct steps for safety. Before backing your tractor under the trailer, lock the trailer brakes.

questions.question: All trailers made after ____ must be equipped with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: When coupling:

options.text: You can assume all vehicles are the same.
Be sure that you are coupling correctly.
Cracks in the mounting are acceptable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be sure that you are coupling correctly.
questions.explanation: Improper coupling and uncoupling of combination vehicles can be very dangerous.

questions.question: What is a bobtail tractor?

options.text: A tractor that travels faster than the speed limit

questions.explanation: A bobtail tractor is a tractor with no semi-trailer attached. Bobtail tractors are difficult to operate and require extra caution.

questions.question: Push in the trailer air supply control to:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to send air to the trailer. Pull out the trailer air supply control to stop the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: If a load is placed on one side of a trailer, what happens?

options.text: The trailer may lean during turns.
The trailer may have extra support during turns.
The trailer may be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer may lean during turns.
questions.explanation: When weight is on one side of a trailer, it leans to that side. This increases the risk of a rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: How many air lines does a combination vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A combination vehicle has two air lines: the service line and the emergency line.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to skid, what should the driver do?
questions.explanation: If your trailer skids while braking, release the brakes. This lets the wheels grip the road again. Once the wheels regain traction, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.

questions.question: If a trailer begins to jackknife, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Allow the wheels to grip the road.
Allow the trailer to straighten out.

questions.explanation: If your trailer jackknifes, release the brakes and let the wheels grip the road. Do not apply the trailer hand brake because it will make the skid worse. The locked brakes caused the problem in the first place.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: Regularly to activate the trailer brakes in all driving conditions.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid.
Only if the trailer is carrying a load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Use the trailer hand valve only to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while driving because it can cause the trailer to skid.

questions.question: What happens if you use the trailer hand valve while driving?

options.text: It will help you turn safely.
It will stop your trailer safely.

questions.explanation: Never use the trailer hand valve while driving. Using it while operating your vehicle can cause your trailer to skid.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: If you need to back your trailer but cannot back straight, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, what is true?

options.text: Most of the weight should be in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: A lightly loaded vehicle may have poor traction. The wheels can lock up easily when you brake a lightly loaded vehicle.

questions.question: What does rearward amplification mean?

options.text: The amount of noise at the rear of a vehicle.
The number of trailers a tractor can pull.

questions.explanation: Vehicles with trailers can roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect, which is caused by rearward amplification.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if the pressure gets too low.
